title: Dense pairwise complements in a finite closed cover give distinct components
statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space and let $I$ be a finite index set. For every $i\in I$ let $E_i\subseteq T$ be a nonempty closed subset. Assume $T= igcup_{i\in I}E_i$ and that, for every $i
e j$, the subset $E_i\setminus E_j$ is dense in $E_i$ in its subspace topology (its closure in $E_i$ is all of $E_i$). There exist points $x_i\in T$ and irreducible components $K_i$ of $T$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], indexed by $I$, such that $x_i\in K_i\subseteq E_i$ and $x_i
otin E_j$ whenever $j
e i$, and the components $K_i$ are pairwise distinct. In particular the assignment $i\mapsto K_i$ is an injection from $I$ into the set of irreducible components of $T$. Empty $I$ is allowed, in which case the covering hypothesis forces $T=\varnothing$ and the conclusion uses the empty families. The pieces $E_i$ need not be irreducible, and no Noetherianity or separation condition on $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, the cover says $T=\varnothing$. Take the empty families of points and components; all containment and distinctness assertions are vacuous and the empty map is injective. Henceforth assume $I\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0554 (lemma-irreducible-components-in-neighbourhood), proof, final topological implication, with the earlier nowhere-dense intersection hypothesis retained

proof.text: Fix $i\in I$ and enumerate $I\setminus\{i\}$ as $j_1,\ldots,j_m$. In the subspace $E_i$, each $O_r=E_i\setminus E_{j_r}$ is open because $E_{j_r}$ is closed in $T$, and is dense by hypothesis. Starting with the nonempty open $W_0=E_i$, put $W_r=W_{r-1}\cap O_r$. Inductively $W_r$ is open and nonempty: otherwise the closed complement of the nonempty open $W_{r-1}$ would contain $O_r$, hence its closure $E_i$, a contradiction. Thus choose $x_i\in W_m$. For $m=0$ use $W_m=E_i$. Choose these points for all $i$; then $x_i\in E_i$ and $x_i\notin E_j$ for every $j\ne i$.

source.place: Tag 0554 (lemma-irreducible-components-in-neighbourhood), proof, final topological implication, with the earlier nowhere-dense intersection hypothesis retained

proof.text: For each chosen $x_i$, apply [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] to the topological space $T$. Its pointwise clause supplies an irreducible component $K_i$ of $T$ containing $x_i$. Choose one such component for every $i$. This applies to arbitrary topological spaces and requires no Noetherianity, generic point or separation assumption.

By [def-weil-irreducible-components], $K_i$ is nonempty and irreducible. The sets $K_i\cap E_j$ form a finite closed cover of $K_i$. The binary closed-cover definition extends to this cover by induction on its size: a cover of size zero is impossible by nonemptiness; for positive size separate its first closed member from the finite union of the others, apply irreducibility, and if the latter equals $K_i$ apply the induction hypothesis to the remaining members. Hence $K_i\subseteq E_j$ for some $j$. Since $x_i\in K_i$ but $x_i\notin E_j$ for $j\ne i$, this index must be $i$, proving $x_i\in K_i\subseteq E_i$.

source.place: Tag 004V (definition-irreducible-components), binary closed-cover definition; finite induction as in Tag 0G2Y (lemma-pick-irreducible-components), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: If $i\ne j$ and $K_i=K_j$, then $x_i\in K_i=K_j\subseteq E_j$, contradicting Step 2. Thus the components are pairwise distinct, and $i\mapsto K_i$ is an injection into the set of irreducible components of $T$. Together with Steps 2--4 this proves every clause.

Step 5 gets distinctness and the injection from Step 2. lean.statement: theorem exists_injective_components_of_closed_cover_dense_complements {T : Type u} [TopologicalSpace T] {I : Type v} [Finite I] (E : I → Set T) (h_nonempty : ∀ i : I, (E i).Nonempty) (h_closed : ∀ i : I, IsClosed (E i)) (h_cover : (⋃ i : I, E i) = Set.univ) (h_dense : ∀ i j : I, i ≠ j → Dense {x : E i | (x : T) ∉ E j}) : ∃ (x : I → T) (K : I → irreducibleComponents T), (∀ i : I, x i ∈ (K i : Set T) ∧ (K i : Set T) ⊆ E i ∧ ∀ j : I, j ≠ i → x i ∉ E j) ∧ Function.Injective K
